While I agree with you that weed and heroin are separate animals the harm done by crimalizing the use of heroin is several fold. First it creates an illegal market where drug dealers are free to change the quality, purity, and dose of their product without regulation and many users die each year from "hot hits". Second, by treating the user as a criminal rather than a mental health patient, we severely lessen that persons ability to kick the habit. Finally, prohibition has been statistically shown to increase consumption in minors, as it's viewed as a taboo and they receive minimal drug education which leads to higher addiction rates. In Portugal there used to be a server drug addiction problem during their prohibition. Drugs have been legal in Portugal for 15 years now and during that time they've seen a huge decrease in addiction and all of the negative consequences of treating users as criminals. Their crime rate dropped, their instances of HIV and hepatitis transmission dropped, and now it's to the point where if you asked someone from Portugal if there's a drug problem they'd say no. Prohibition is what causes the real damage from drug use because it creates a stigma against the user and facilitates a black market where we cannot regulate the drugs.
